title: Consumption mask parity: re-randomise on every display flush, DMA-fed TRNG duty table on a secure GPDMA channel, and put an actual load on the mask pin
threat: Trace alignment on frame transmission: the attacker aligns a power/EM trace on the SPI frame (the moment content-dependent current/EM appears). pq1's mask is re-randomised only from the secure tick, from a xorshift PRNG, and drives an NC pad, so it neither decorrelates per frame nor demonstrably dilutes anything.
proposal: (1) Call `hw::consumption_mask::randomize()` at the top of `lcd::Display::flush` / `flush_with_secret_rows` and in `px::lcd::present_frame_ex` before the first strip goes out (Trezor's `display_refresh` hook), drawing that sample from rng_strong rather than the xorshift. (2) Port Trezor's DMA-fed table: a 119-entry duty table in S-SRAM refreshed from the TRNG, GPDMA1 channel in circular linked-list mode triggered by TIMx_UP writing CCR1 every 100 us, with the channel configured SEC|PRIV|SRC_SEC|DEST_SEC so NS cannot halt it (the module header already lists this as the follow-up). (3) EVT: route the mask pin (pq1 PA6, currently NC) to a small resistive load across the 3V3 near the die so the duty cycle actually modulates supply current; then measure dilution with the SCA bench (TVLA before/after) and close the 'unmeasured' caveat.
rationale: Direct Trezor parity on the same MCU family; (1) is a two-line change, (3) is the only thing that makes the production-mandatory fence mean something. Without (3) the feature is satisfied-by-construction, as CLAUDE.md admits.
repo_evidence: secure/src/main.rs:4337 (the ONLY `consumption_mask::randomize()` call — periodic tick); grep randomize in secure/src/ui/lcd.rs, secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs, secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs: none
secure/src/hw/consumption_mask.rs:12-20 ('A full DMA port is a follow-up'), :41-51 (neither board drives a load; dilution unmeasured), :166-192 (randomize from xorshift32)
gh #831 OPEN priority:medium (reseed fails open, biased toward signing windows); gh #646 OPEN
vendor_precedent: Trezor core/embed/io/display/vg-2864/display_driver.c:407-425 (`consumption_mask_randomize()` on every display_refresh); core/embed/sec/consumption_mask/stm32u5/consumption_mask.c:73-142 (GPDMA1 linked-list, TIM2_UP trigger, SEC|PRIV channel attributes at :85-87,117-118).
risks: Trezor only enables the mask on OLED models and has no mask on TFT — its 'no mask on TFT' choice is not evidence that pq1's SPI TFT is safe (different channel: bus EM, not row current). A loaded pin costs a few mA continuously. The GPDMA channel must be verified blocked from NS on silicon (#53 still open). Per-frame randomisation adds a TRNG read per frame — bound it so it cannot stall the frame.
